_comment: Hand-written: the expert groups of each golem-fx pedal, in the block sheet's order. The front panel is the pedal face (faces.json); every other parameter sits in exactly one group. `custom` is the bool parameter that unlocks the group (its params greyed until it is on); null when the group has none. Checked by tools/build-descriptors.py against the code. `help` gives the one-line help of parameters whose documentation table leaves the role empty. `depends` greys a parameter that only acts in one mode (the builder checks the value is an option). Factory presets live in presets/<crate>.json.

gfx-comp.thresh: Level above which the compressor starts to reduce gain
gfx-comp.attack: How fast gain reduction sets in once the level exceeds the threshold
gfx-comp.ratio: How much the level above the threshold is reduced (30:1 ≈ limiting)
gfx-comp.character: The compressor's voicing: clean, bus glue, FET, opto or pedal

gfx-eq.mid2freq: Centre frequency of the second mid band
gfx-eq.airfreq: Corner frequency of the air shelf
gfx-eq.harsh_freq: Centre of the band the de-harsher watches and tames
gfx-eq.lowcut: High-pass filter: removes the lows below this frequency
gfx-eq.midgain: Boost or cut of the mid bell
gfx-eq.harsh_range: Maximum cut the de-harsher may apply

gfx-deesser.shape: How the sibilance is cut: high shelf, narrow bell or wide band

gfx-wah.model: The wah circuit whose sweep, Q and voicing are played
gfx-wah.mix: Wet level against the dry signal (100 % = wah only)
gfx-wah.mode: Manual = the pedal sweeps; auto = the envelope sweeps; alien = both
gfx-wah.taper: How the pedal travel maps onto the sweep; Model = the circuit's own pot
gfx-wah.toe: Where the sweep ends at toe down (percent of the full range)
gfx-wah.auto_engage: Switches the wah on when the pedal moves, off when it rests at heel
gfx-wah.engage_wait: How long the pedal must rest at heel before the wah switches off
gfx-wah.env_sens: How strongly playing dynamics move the sweep (auto and alien modes)
gfx-wah.env_att: How fast the envelope follows a louder note
gfx-wah.env_rel: How fast the envelope falls back after the note

gfx-autowah.poles: Filter slope: 2 poles = vocal, 4 poles = deeper, synth-like
gfx-autowah.direction: Up = louder notes sweep upward; Down = they sweep downward
gfx-autowah.attack: How fast the sweep follows a picked note
gfx-autowah.release: How fast the sweep falls back after the note
gfx-autowah.mix: Wet level against the dry signal (100 % = filter only)
gfx-autowah.source: What moves the filter: playing dynamics, an LFO, sample and hold, or both
gfx-autowah.sync: Locks the LFO to the host tempo; Off = the Rate control
gfx-autowah.peak: Resonance of the filter: higher = a sharper, more vocal peak
gfx-autowah.rate: Speed of the LFO or sample-and-hold source

gfx-tremolo.rate: Speed of the volume modulation (when Sync is Off)
gfx-tremolo.model: The tremolo circuit: clean VCA, valve bias, optical cell, neon or harmonic (two bands in opposition)
gfx-tremolo.sync: Locks the rate to the host tempo; Off = the Rate control
gfx-tremolo.xover: Split frequency of the Harmonic model's two bands

gfx-vibrato.speed: Speed of the pitch modulation (when Sync is Off)
gfx-vibrato.model: The vibrato circuit: clean delay, BBD, varistor, Uni-Vibe-style or organ scanner
gfx-vibrato.sync: Locks the speed to the host tempo; Off = the Speed control
gfx-vibrato.tone: Low-pass after the vibrato: darker as it rises

gfx-flanger.rate: Speed of the sweep (when Sync is Off)
gfx-flanger.mode: The flanger voicing: classic pedals, tape through-zero, barber-pole or pedal-controlled
gfx-flanger.fb_polarity: Sign of the feedback: + = metallic peaks, − = hollow notches
gfx-flanger.sweep_src: What sweeps the delay: the LFO, playing dynamics, the Manual control, or LFO and dynamics
gfx-flanger.env_sens: Level at which playing dynamics start to move the sweep
gfx-flanger.env_att: How fast the envelope follows a louder note
gfx-flanger.env_rel: How fast the envelope falls back after the note
gfx-flanger.stereo_phase: LFO offset between left and right (180° = opposite sweeps)
gfx-flanger.fb_hpf: High-pass in the feedback loop: keeps the lows from building up
gfx-flanger.fb_lpf: Low-pass in the feedback loop: softens the resonance

gfx-phaser.rate: Speed of the sweep (when Sync is Off)
gfx-phaser.model: The phaser voicing: classic pedals, Uni-Vibe-style, dual or barber-pole
gfx-phaser.fb_polarity: Sign of the feedback: + = sharper peaks, − = hollow notches
gfx-phaser.depth: How much of the frequency range the sweep covers
gfx-phaser.skew: Tilts the LFO so the sweep rises and falls at different speeds (50 % = symmetric)
gfx-phaser.sweep_src: What sweeps the stages: the LFO, playing dynamics, the Manual control, or LFO and dynamics
gfx-phaser.env_sens: How strongly playing dynamics move the sweep
gfx-phaser.env_att: How fast the envelope follows a louder note
gfx-phaser.env_rel: How fast the envelope falls back after the note
gfx-phaser.feedback: Resonance of the stages (closer to 0 dB = more pronounced)
gfx-phaser.lamp_lag: Response time of the Vibe model's lamp: smoother sweep as it rises

gfx-rotary.cabinet: The rotary cabinet model: speaker sizes, horn and drum voicing
gfx-rotary.balance: Level between the horn (treble) and the drum (bass)
gfx-rotary.horn_decel: Time the horn takes to slow down from Fast to Slow
gfx-rotary.drum_accel: Time the heavier drum takes to speed up to Fast
gfx-rotary.drum_decel: Time the drum takes to slow down from Fast to Slow
gfx-rotary.drive: Tube preamp drive before the speakers
gfx-rotary.horn_accel: Time the horn takes to speed up to Fast

gfx-delay.duck_thresh: Playing level above which the repeats duck
gfx-delay.ratio: Right delay time as a multiple of the left one (Dual stereo mode)
gfx-delay.bypass: Bypass switch that lets the repeats ring out when Trails is on
gfx-delay.trails: When bypassed, let the repeats already in the loop fade out naturally
gfx-delay.model: The delay medium: digital, tape, bucket-brigade or lo-fi
gfx-delay.width: Stereo width of the repeats (the dry stays as it is)

gfx-reverb.bass_xover: Frequency below which Bass Mult scales the decay
gfx-reverb.diffusion: How quickly the echoes blur into a smooth tail
gfx-reverb.width: Stereo width of the tail (above 100 % = wider than the room)
gfx-reverb.duck: How much the tail drops while you play
gfx-reverb.duck_release: How fast the tail comes back once you stop
gfx-reverb.kill_dry: Mutes the direct signal, for parallel routing
gfx-reverb.bypass: Bypass switch that lets the tail ring out when Trails is on
gfx-reverb.trails: When bypassed, let the tail already in the room decay naturally
gfx-reverb.decay: Time the tail takes to fall by 60 dB in the mid band
gfx-reverb.size: Size of the room: longer early reflections and a bigger tail
gfx-reverb.springs: Number of springs in the Spring algorithm

gfx-shimmer.voice2: Level of the second pitch voice
gfx-shimmer.trails: When bypassed, let the tail decay naturally
gfx-shimmer.bypass: Bypass switch that lets the tail ring out when Trails is on
gfx-shimmer.decay: Time the tail takes to fall by 60 dB in the mid band
gfx-shimmer.pitch2: Interval of the second pitch voice
gfx-shimmer.detune: Detunes the two sides apart for a wider, chorused shimmer
gfx-shimmer.size: Scale of the reverb tank: bigger = slower, wider space
gfx-shimmer.bass_mult: Low-frequency decay relative to the mid band
gfx-shimmer.kill_dry: Mutes the direct signal, for a parallel lane

gfx-killswitch.depth: How far the signal drops when cut (100 % = silence)
gfx-killswitch.sync: Note value of the stutter at the host tempo; Free = the Rate control
gfx-killswitch.trigger: What starts the stutter: engaging the pedal, each pick attack, or the beat
gfx-killswitch.shape: Envelope of each cut: hard gate or a smoother waveform
gfx-killswitch.swing: Delays every other step for a shuffled rhythm
gfx-killswitch.sens: Sensitivity of the pick detector (Trigger = Pick)

gfx-octaver.octave1: Level of the voice one octave below
gfx-octaver.octave2: Level of the voice two octaves below
gfx-octaver.octave_up: Level of the voice one octave above
gfx-octaver.mode: Tracking engine and character: vintage analog, clean, synth-like or polyphonic
gfx-octaver.up_tone: Low-pass on the octave-up voice: tames its harshness
gfx-octaver.glide: Pitch glide between notes, for a synth-like octave

gfx-pitch.voice2: Level of the second pitch voice

gfx-limiter.style: How peaks are held: clean, punchy (faster release) or clip (soft clipping)

gfx-chorus.delay_base: Centre delay the modulation swings around

gfx-drive.voice: The clipping circuit: overdrive, distortion, fuzz or golem's legacy curve

gfx-geq.g2: Octave 11 fader at 60 Hz: the EQ's gain there, in dB

gfx-geq.g4: Octave 11 fader at 250 Hz: the EQ's gain there, in dB

gfx-geq.g9: Octave 11 fader at 8 kHz: the EQ's gain there, in dB
gfx-geq.g10: Octave 11 fader at 12 kHz: the EQ's gain there, in dB
gfx-geq.g11: Octave 11 fader at 16 kHz: the EQ's gain there, in dB

gfx-geq.gt_400: Guitar 7 fader at 400 Hz: the EQ's gain there, in dB

gfx-geq.gt_3k2: Guitar 7 fader at 3.2 kHz: the EQ's gain there, in dB
gfx-geq.gt_6k4: Guitar 7 fader at 6.4 kHz: the EQ's gain there, in dB
gfx-geq.gb_50: Bass 7 fader at 50 Hz: the EQ's gain there, in dB
gfx-geq.gb_120: Bass 7 fader at 120 Hz: the EQ's gain there, in dB
gfx-geq.gb_400: Bass 7 fader at 400 Hz: the EQ's gain there, in dB
gfx-geq.gb_500: Bass 7 fader at 500 Hz: the EQ's gain there, in dB
gfx-geq.gb_800: Bass 7 fader at 800 Hz: the EQ's gain there, in dB

gfx-crusher.sync: Locks the rate LFO to the host tempo (Off: Mod Rate sets it)
gfx-crusher.env_sens: How strongly the playing level drives the rate modulation
gfx-crusher.env_att: How fast the envelope follows a rising level
gfx-crusher.env_rel: How fast the envelope falls back after a note

gfx-ringmod.pitch: Carrier = base × this interval (−60 … +60 st), Free and Track: the musical carrier sweep
gfx-ringmod.feedback: mda's recursive ring: the output fed back into the multiplier, cascaded sidebands
gfx-ringmod.thr: Under this level the tracker holds its note and the wet is squelched (0 = never)
gfx-ringmod.speed: Carrier glide between notes (Surge's law, 208 → 24 ms)
gfx-ringmod.env_sens: How loud the playing must be to move the envelope
gfx-ringmod.env_rel: How fast the envelope falls back

gfx-bassdi.low_note: The lowest open string: golem sets it from the lane's tuning; every low corner follows it
gfx-bassdi.bass_keep: Below this frequency the bass stays clean, mono and out of the clipper (0 = off)
gfx-bassdi.cab_lows: Off: the speaker emulation acts only above the bass
gfx-bassdi.comp_path: Dirt: compress the driven path only; Both: compress before the clean / dirt split
gfx-bassdi.sag: 50 % = the model's own sag; 0 = none, 100 % = double (no effect in Modern)
gfx-bassdi.model: Modern: CMOS grind; Classic: tube-emulation DI push; Vintage: valve-preamp grit
gfx-bassdi.lo_mid_freq: Centre of the Lo Mid band (the hardware positions: 250, 500, 1,000 Hz)
gfx-bassdi.hi_mid_freq: Centre of the Hi Mid band, the growl (the hardware positions: 750, 1,500, 3,000 Hz)

gfx-tape.input: How hard the tape is hit: 0 dB puts a -18 dBFS note at the machine's reference; the output stays level
gfx-tape.wow: Peak slow speed deviation (% of speed); the model sets its spectrum
gfx-tape.flutter: Peak fast speed deviation (% of speed), 4 - 200 Hz
gfx-tape.wear: Age and failures in the model's own way: dull heads, dropouts, crinkles, snags or crackle
gfx-tape.bias: Under 100 %: crossover grit and a brighter top; over: cleaner and darker
gfx-tape.spacing: Head-to-tape gap: highs vanish first, much more at low speed
gfx-tape.azimuth: Head tilt in arc-minutes: duller highs; in stereo a delay between the tracks
gfx-tape.wow_rate: Scales the speed of every slow wobble of the transport
gfx-tape.wow_rand: Negative: a regular, machine-like wobble; positive: erratic
gfx-tape.drop_sync: Puts the dropouts on the host grid (Off: random)
gfx-tape.noise_mode: Follow: noise only under the playing; Constant: always; Duck: in the gaps
gfx-tape.stop: Tape stop: the motor winds down; off spins it back up
gfx-tape.spread: Stereo: the random wobble and failures differ left and right

gfx-grit.lo_m1: The low band's first dirt module (slot 1 runs before slot 2)
gfx-grit.lo_v1: Amount of the low band's first module, in that module's own law (dB, bits, Hz, exponent)
gfx-grit.lo_y1: Gain of a Peak module in the low band's slot 1 (a cut before a clipper is a scoop); inert for other types
gfx-grit.lo_m2: The low band's second dirt module (slot 2 runs after slot 1)
gfx-grit.lo_v2: Amount of the low band's second module, in that module's own law (dB, bits, Hz, exponent)
gfx-grit.lo_y2: Gain of a Peak module in the low band's slot 2 (a cut before a clipper is a scoop); inert for other types
gfx-grit.lo_gain: Level of the whole low band after its dirt and mix; −60 dB is a mute
gfx-grit.lo_mix: The low band's own dry / wet, multiplied by Wet: parallel dirt on one band, no comb
gfx-grit.lo_solo: Hear the low band alone (several soloed: their sum); a set-up switch
gfx-grit.lo_bypass: The low band passes clean at 0 dB: its modules, mix and gain are ignored
gfx-grit.lm_m1: The low-mid band's first dirt module (slot 1 runs before slot 2)
gfx-grit.lm_v1: Amount of the low-mid band's first module, in that module's own law (dB, bits, Hz, exponent)
gfx-grit.lm_y1: Gain of a Peak module in the low-mid band's slot 1 (a cut before a clipper is a scoop); inert for other types
gfx-grit.lm_m2: The low-mid band's second dirt module (slot 2 runs after slot 1)
gfx-grit.lm_v2: Amount of the low-mid band's second module, in that module's own law (dB, bits, Hz, exponent)
gfx-grit.lm_y2: Gain of a Peak module in the low-mid band's slot 2 (a cut before a clipper is a scoop); inert for other types
gfx-grit.lm_gain: Level of the whole low-mid band after its dirt and mix; −60 dB is a mute
gfx-grit.lm_mix: The low-mid band's own dry / wet, multiplied by Wet: parallel dirt on one band, no comb
gfx-grit.lm_solo: Hear the low-mid band alone (several soloed: their sum); a set-up switch
gfx-grit.lm_bypass: The low-mid band passes clean at 0 dB: its modules, mix and gain are ignored
gfx-grit.hm_m1: The high-mid band's first dirt module (slot 1 runs before slot 2)
gfx-grit.hm_v1: Amount of the high-mid band's first module, in that module's own law (dB, bits, Hz, exponent)
gfx-grit.hm_y1: Gain of a Peak module in the high-mid band's slot 1 (a cut before a clipper is a scoop); inert for other types
gfx-grit.hm_m2: The high-mid band's second dirt module (slot 2 runs after slot 1)
gfx-grit.hm_v2: Amount of the high-mid band's second module, in that module's own law (dB, bits, Hz, exponent)
gfx-grit.hm_y2: Gain of a Peak module in the high-mid band's slot 2 (a cut before a clipper is a scoop); inert for other types
gfx-grit.hm_gain: Level of the whole high-mid band after its dirt and mix; −60 dB is a mute
gfx-grit.hm_mix: The high-mid band's own dry / wet, multiplied by Wet: parallel dirt on one band, no comb
gfx-grit.hm_solo: Hear the high-mid band alone (several soloed: their sum); a set-up switch
gfx-grit.hm_bypass: The high-mid band passes clean at 0 dB: its modules, mix and gain are ignored
gfx-grit.hi_m1: The high band's first dirt module (slot 1 runs before slot 2)
gfx-grit.hi_v1: Amount of the high band's first module, in that module's own law (dB, bits, Hz, exponent)
gfx-grit.hi_y1: Gain of a Peak module in the high band's slot 1 (a cut before a clipper is a scoop); inert for other types
gfx-grit.hi_m2: The high band's second dirt module (slot 2 runs after slot 1)
gfx-grit.hi_v2: Amount of the high band's second module, in that module's own law (dB, bits, Hz, exponent)
gfx-grit.hi_y2: Gain of a Peak module in the high band's slot 2 (a cut before a clipper is a scoop); inert for other types
gfx-grit.hi_gain: Level of the whole high band after its dirt and mix; −60 dB is a mute
gfx-grit.hi_mix: The high band's own dry / wet, multiplied by Wet: parallel dirt on one band, no comb
gfx-grit.hi_solo: Hear the high band alone (several soloed: their sum); a set-up switch
gfx-grit.hi_bypass: The high band passes clean at 0 dB: its modules, mix and gain are ignored

gfx-mbcomp.lo_thresh: Downward threshold of the low band, RMS-calibrated; Tilt moves it
gfx-mbcomp.lo_ratio: Downward ratio of the low band (gfx-comp's meaning); Amount scales its slope
gfx-mbcomp.lo_lift_thresh: Below this level Lift works on the low band; held at or under the threshold
gfx-mbcomp.lo_lift: Slope below the Lift threshold: + lifts quiet parts (+75 % = 4:1 upward), − expands (−100 % = 1:2)
gfx-mbcomp.lo_attack: How fast the gain of the low band moves down; scaled by Time
gfx-mbcomp.lo_release: How fast the gain of the low band moves back up; scaled by Time
gfx-mbcomp.lo_gain: Static level of the low band on top of the make-up: phase-free band EQ
gfx-mbcomp.lo_sc: What the detector of the low band hears: its own band, or the whole input (Wide)
gfx-mbcomp.lm_thresh: Downward threshold of the low-mid band (Mid), RMS-calibrated; Tilt moves it
gfx-mbcomp.lm_ratio: Downward ratio of the low-mid band (Mid) (gfx-comp's meaning); Amount scales its slope
gfx-mbcomp.lm_lift_thresh: Below this level Lift works on the low-mid band (Mid); held at or under the threshold
gfx-mbcomp.lm_lift: Slope below the Lift threshold: + lifts quiet parts (+75 % = 4:1 upward), − expands (−100 % = 1:2)
gfx-mbcomp.lm_attack: How fast the gain of the low-mid band (Mid) moves down; scaled by Time
gfx-mbcomp.lm_release: How fast the gain of the low-mid band (Mid) moves back up; scaled by Time
gfx-mbcomp.lm_gain: Static level of the low-mid band (Mid) on top of the make-up: phase-free band EQ
gfx-mbcomp.lm_sc: What the detector of the low-mid band (Mid) hears: its own band, or the whole input (Wide)
gfx-mbcomp.hm_thresh: Downward threshold of the high-mid band, RMS-calibrated; Tilt moves it
gfx-mbcomp.hm_ratio: Downward ratio of the high-mid band (gfx-comp's meaning); Amount scales its slope
gfx-mbcomp.hm_lift_thresh: Below this level Lift works on the high-mid band; held at or under the threshold
gfx-mbcomp.hm_lift: Slope below the Lift threshold: + lifts quiet parts (+75 % = 4:1 upward), − expands (−100 % = 1:2)
gfx-mbcomp.hm_attack: How fast the gain of the high-mid band moves down; scaled by Time
gfx-mbcomp.hm_release: How fast the gain of the high-mid band moves back up; scaled by Time
gfx-mbcomp.hm_gain: Static level of the high-mid band on top of the make-up: phase-free band EQ
gfx-mbcomp.hm_sc: What the detector of the high-mid band hears: its own band, or the whole input (Wide)
gfx-mbcomp.hi_thresh: Downward threshold of the high band, RMS-calibrated; Tilt moves it
gfx-mbcomp.hi_ratio: Downward ratio of the high band (gfx-comp's meaning); Amount scales its slope
gfx-mbcomp.hi_lift_thresh: Below this level Lift works on the high band; held at or under the threshold
gfx-mbcomp.hi_lift: Slope below the Lift threshold: + lifts quiet parts (+75 % = 4:1 upward), − expands (−100 % = 1:2)
gfx-mbcomp.hi_attack: How fast the gain of the high band moves down; scaled by Time
gfx-mbcomp.hi_release: How fast the gain of the high band moves back up; scaled by Time
gfx-mbcomp.hi_gain: Static level of the high band on top of the make-up: phase-free band EQ
gfx-mbcomp.hi_sc: What the detector of the high band hears: its own band, or the whole input (Wide)
gfx-mbcomp.bypass: True bypass to the input (delayed by the latency in Linear), 10 ms crossfade
gfx-mbcomp.bands: 3 or 4 bands: 4 adds the High Mid band and the Mid crossover (a set-up switch, crossfaded in 40 ms)

gfx-widener.mode: The side generator: Velvet (fine, irregular width), Allpass (no smear, broad colour), Comb (pseudo-stereo), Double (micro-shift), M/S (a stereo source's own width only)
gfx-widener.amount: Level of the generated side re the mid; 100 % = correlation 0 on a mono source
gfx-widener.width: Master side gain (source side and generated); 0 % = mono, 100 % = neutral for a stereo source
gfx-widener.time: Velvet length (10 - 40 ms), Comb delay, Double delay; inert in Allpass and M/S
gfx-widener.bass_keep: Below it the output is mono and dry (a high-pass on the side only); 0 = off
gfx-widener.mono_law: Exact: the mono fold is the dry. Classic: true Haas (Comb) and L / R voices (Double); inert elsewhere
gfx-widener.variant: Which velvet sequence or all-pass set: two lanes on two variants stay distinct
gfx-widener.cents: Double: each voice is shifted up and down by this much
gfx-widener.high_cut: Low-pass on the generated side only: keeps sibilants and pick noise centred
gfx-widener.transient: Ducks the generated side on attacks: the pick stays centred, the sustain blooms wide
gfx-widener.balance: Places the image (positive = right) without touching the mono fold
gfx-widener.rotate: Rotates a stereo image (positive = right); moves the mono fold
gfx-widener.listen: Audition the mono fold or the side alone (not stored by golem)

gfx-tuner.string_1: Custom tuning's open string 1 (MIDI, 1 = the lowest); 0 ends the list
gfx-tuner.offset_1: Sweetening of string 1 in cents (1 = the lowest), its 12th-fret harmonic included
gfx-tuner.string_2: Custom tuning's open string 2 (MIDI, 1 = the lowest); 0 ends the list

gfx-correct.m09: Note mask: A allowed as a target (intersected with key / scale; written by golem's compile)
gfx-correct.m10: Note mask: A# allowed as a target (intersected with key / scale; written by golem's compile)
gfx-correct.m11: Note mask: B allowed as a target (intersected with key / scale; written by golem's compile)

gfx-acoustic.body: The body's resonances (the boom, the breath): 50 % = the model's own, ±12 dB
gfx-acoustic.top: Attack and sparkle, and the trim for a guitar that is not the pickup guess: 50 % = the model's own
gfx-acoustic.mic: Microphone blend: 0 bridge, 50 sound hole, 100 neck (12th – 14th fret)
gfx-acoustic.decay: Shortens the electric's sustain as an acoustic body drains the strings: 50 % = the model's own, 0 = off
gfx-acoustic.pickup: The guitar's pickup, so its EMF can be rebuilt from the DI (golem sets it at insert)
gfx-acoustic.piezo: Adds an under-saddle piezo voice to the mic: the stage sound
gfx-acoustic.quack: Piezo source only: tames the piezo's mid peak on the attacks
gfx-acoustic.width: 2 / 2 only: the spacing of the two microphones

gfx-grains.trails: With bypass: on, the cloud finishes its grains and a hold releases in its decay; off, the wet fades out in 20 ms

gfx-sustainer.mode: Feedback: one harmonic blooms out of the note · Sustain: every partial held at its level · Both: the note held, its harmonic blooming on it

gfx-polysynth.engine: Spectral: every partial of the guitar turned into a waveform, polyphonic, instant, no tracking · Mono: one synth voice on the note, glide and exact bends, the attack bridged by Spectral
gfx-polysynth.wave: Saw · Pulse (50 % = square) · Triangle · Sine: the oscillators (Mono) and the waveform of every band (Spectral)
gfx-polysynth.amp_mode: Follow: the string's own level, flattened by Hold · Gate: an ADSR from every pick
gfx-polysynth.bank: Dual: fast bank on attacks, legato and bends, clean bank on held notes · Fast: tightest, chords gritty · Clean: cleanest chords, slow attack (pads)
gfx-polysynth.quantize: Off: bends and vibrato pass · Chromatic: the nearest semitone, held with hysteresis (Mono)

gfx-spectralcomp.thresh: Band level (a sine's dBFS in its band) at Center where the work starts; the same reading at every window
gfx-spectralcomp.down: Downward ratio above the threshold curve, per band; 1 = off
gfx-spectralcomp.up: Upward ratio below the curve, never under the noise guard; 1 = off
gfx-spectralcomp.slope: Tilts the threshold about Center in dB per octave; 0 is flat for pink noise, negative holds the highs sooner
gfx-spectralcomp.attack: How fast a rising band is held; the window adds a quarter to a half of its length
gfx-spectralcomp.mode: Live: zero latency, two-thirds-octave bells. Studio: per bin inside the STFT, latency of the window. Set before playing
gfx-spectralcomp.release: How fast a falling band is let go
gfx-spectralcomp.window: Analysis size (samples at 48 kHz): longer resolves lower notes, reacts later; Studio's latency. Set before playing
gfx-spectralcomp.res: Width of each bin's detector band (semitones): wider is smoother, less musical noise; 0 = the main lobe
gfx-spectralcomp.knee: Quadratic knee around the threshold, both directions
gfx-spectralcomp.guard: Nothing at or under this level is lifted: the upward stage never raises hiss
gfx-spectralcomp.source: What the detector reads: the lane itself, or the key (the lane's DI today); no key = no change
gfx-spectralcomp.auto_gain: Static make-up from the settings (pink noise at -18 dBFS RMS matches bypass); 0 dB under a key
gfx-spectralcomp.mix: Dry / wet, the dry aligned to the wet
gfx-spectralcomp.link: Stereo: each channel's band levels move toward the louder one's
gfx-spectralcomp.delta: Hear only what the compressor changes (wet minus dry)
gfx-spectralcomp.bypass: The dry, still delayed in Studio so the lane's latency stays

gfx-morph.low_a: Low band (the chest, under the low crossover): the band's dirt type (Off, Soft, Hard, Tube, Fuzz, Rectify, Fold, Sine Fold, Crush, Decimate, Sputter, Ring, Carbon, Starve, Rasp) at morph 0 %
gfx-morph.body_a: Body band (the vowel; the whole voice in Single): the band's dirt type (Off, Soft, Hard, Tube, Fuzz, Rectify, Fold, Sine Fold, Crush, Decimate, Sputter, Ring, Carbon, Starve, Rasp) at morph 0 %
gfx-morph.air_a: Air band (sibilance and breath, over the air crossover): the band's dirt type (Off, Soft, Hard, Tube, Fuzz, Rectify, Fold, Sine Fold, Crush, Decimate, Sputter, Ring, Carbon, Starve, Rasp) at morph 0 %
gfx-morph.low_b: Low band's type at morph 100 %: the morph blends A into B, level-held
gfx-morph.body_b: Body band's type at morph 100 %: the morph blends A into B, level-held
gfx-morph.air_b: Air band's type at morph 100 %: the morph blends A into B, level-held
gfx-morph.low_trim: Added to the low band's drive (dB)
gfx-morph.body_trim: Added to the body band's drive (dB); in Single it is a second drive control
gfx-morph.air_trim: Added to the air band's drive (dB)
gfx-morph.low_level: The whole low band after the mix; -60 = mute
gfx-morph.body_level: The whole body band after the mix, into the box and the comp; -60 = mute
gfx-morph.air_level: The whole air band after the mix; -60 = mute
gfx-morph.guard: Loop-gain cap threshold (dBFS RMS): under it the pedal is quieter than bypass at every frequency; -90 = off. Set at soundcheck about 10 dB over the bleed, watching the state lamp
gfx-morph.defizz: Lowers the drive while an 's' passes, then shelves its band down: up to 18 dB; 0 for guitar and drums
gfx-morph.order: Dirt → Box: a distorted voice heard through the object; Box → Dirt: the object's peaks clip first
gfx-morph.object_b: The object morph target; Same = no object morph (morph moves the dirt only)
gfx-morph.env_drive: The voice's envelope (10 ms RMS, -48 to -12 dBFS) into the drive: + louder singing distorts more, - the dirt backs off on loud notes
gfx-morph.env_morph: The envelope added to morph: louder singing moves toward type B and object B
gfx-morph.env_filter: The envelope moves the post high cut by up to ±4 octaves: a talking filter
gfx-morph.echo_time: The slap's delay (ms), gliding when moved
gfx-morph.echo_fb: The slap's repeats, through a 4 kHz low-pass in the loop
gfx-morph.level: Output level (dB), after everything; presets are level-matched with it
